DOAS: Double Observer Adjusted Survey

The DOAS R package provides a unified Frequentist and Hierarchical Bayesian statistical framework to estimate wildlife population abundance from either full Double Observer (DO) surveys (100% of sectors surveyed by two observers) or partial Double Observer Adjusted Surveys (DOAS) that combine targeted DO surveys in a subset of sectors with single-observer block counts across the remaining study area.

By calibrating detection probability on the Double Observer sectors—and optionally modeling both detection covariates (p_formula) and habitat/abundance covariates (n_formula)—DOAS corrects for imperfect detection (p<1p < 1) across entire landscapes while substantially reducing field personnel requirements.

Installation

You can install the development version of DOAS from GitHub using devtools:

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("achazhardenberg/DOAS", build_vignettes = TRUE)

Overview of Features

1. Flexible Data Ingestion & Validation

  • doas_data(): Validates and standardizes survey data from three field recording formats into a doas_data object (with a dedicated print() summary):
    • format = "sector": Wide sector-level summaries (total_count, detected_groups, groups_both, groups_obs1, groups_obs2). Automatically infers detected_groups or groups_both if one is omitted in DO sectors, retains all sector-level covariate columns, and flags sectors with total_count = NA as "Unsurveyed" for prediction via n_formula.
    • format = "group": Long group-level capture histories (one row per detected animal group with obs1 and obs2 binary detection indicators).
    • format = "sighting": Long observer-sighting records reconciled by group_id and observer.

2. Frequentist & Hierarchical Bayesian Abundance Estimators

  • doas(): Core abundance estimator supporting both full Double Observer surveys and partial DOAS designs via orthogonal arguments:
    • method = c("frequentist", "bayesian"): Choose between Frequentist estimation (with analytical multivariate Delta-method or non-parametric spatial block "bootstrap" confidence intervals) and pure-R multi-chain Hierarchical Bayesian MCMC estimation (reporting posterior means, 95% credible intervals, Gelman–Rubin R̂\hat{R}, and effective sample size neffn_{\text{eff}}).
    • obs_type = c("independent", "dependent"): Supports both simultaneous independent observers (Chapman mark–recapture with symmetric observer pool efficiency p‾=(p1+p2)/2\bar{p} = (p_1 + p_2)/2) and dependent primary–secondary observer protocols (Zippin removal).
    • pooling = c("hybrid", "global"): "hybrid" (default) retains direct mark–recapture estimates inside surveyed DO sectors and extrapolates only single-observer Block sectors; "global" applies the calibrated single-observer detection rate across all surveyed sectors.
    • p_formula = ~ ...: Models sector-level variation in detection probability using standard R linear model formulas (supporting multiple covariates, interaction terms such as ~ effort * ruggedness, and polynomial terms).
    • n_formula = ~ ...: Models sector-level abundance (log⁡λi=𝒛i⊤𝜸\log \lambda_i = \mathbf{z}_i^\top \boldsymbol{\gamma}) as a function of environmental covariates (e.g., ~ elevation + habitat + offset(log(area))), automatically imputing any unsurveyed sectors (total_count = NA).
  • predict.doas(): S3 predict() method that predicts sector abundance (type = "abundance"), group count (type = "groups"), or detection probability (type = "detection") with standard errors and 95% confidence/credible intervals for in-sample sectors or new covariate grids (newdata).
  • Low-Level Building Blocks:
    • chapman_estimate() & chapman_variance(): Bias-corrected independent double-observer estimator and Seber (1982) variance.
    • dependent_zippin_estimate() & dependent_zippin_variance(): Primary–secondary observer removal estimator and variance.
    • bayesian_conjugate_estimate(): Bound-safe multi-chain conjugate Beta–Binomial MCMC abundance estimator for DO sectors.

3. Information-Theoretic Model Selection

  • QAIC(): Computes the Quasi-Akaike Information Criterion (ĉ\hat{c}, KK, ΔQAIC\Delta\text{QAIC}) to rank competing frequentist doas detection (p_formula) or abundance (n_formula) models while accounting for overdispersion.
  • WAIC(): Computes the Widely Applicable Information Criterion (lppd\text{lppd}, pWAICp_{\text{WAIC}}, ΔWAIC\Delta\text{WAIC}) from the pointwise posterior log-likelihood matrix of Bayesian doas models.

4. Simulation & Prospective Power Analysis

  • simulate_pop(): Generates spatially structured animal populations partitioned into groups across sectors.
  • simulate_survey(): Simulates full DO or partial DOAS surveys with group-size scaling, counting error, inter-observer skill differences (obs_effect), inter-sector heterogeneity (detvar), and sector covariate effects (cov_effect).
  • doas_power(): Conducts Monte Carlo power and accuracy analyses across varying numbers of Double Observer sectors (surv_areas) for any combination of method, obs_type, pooling, p_formula, and n_formula.

Quick Start Example 

library(DOAS)

# 1. Simulate a 24-sector population (~3500 animals) with a habitat effect on abundance,
#    and a partial DOAS survey (12 DO sectors, 12 Block sectors) with an effort effect on detection
set.seed(12)
pop <- simulate_pop(
  pop_size   = 3500,
  mean_group = 8,
  tot_areas  = 24,
  n_formula  = ~ habitat,
  n_betas    = c(habitat = 0.5)
)
raw_data <- simulate_survey(
  sim_pop         = pop,
  det_p1          = 0.55,
  intra_group_det = 1.0,
  det_group       = 0.95,
  obs_effect      = 0.90,
  detvar          = 0.02,
  surv_areas      = 12,
  p_formula       = ~ effort,
  p_betas         = c(effort = 1.0)
)

survey_dat <- doas_data(raw_data, format = "sector")
print(head(survey_dat))

# 2. Maximum Likelihood (ML) Estimation (Detection & Abundance Covariates)
fit_ml_cov <- doas(
  survey_dat,
  method    = "ML",
  obs_type  = "independent",
  pooling   = "hybrid",
  p_formula = ~ effort,
  n_formula = ~ habitat
)

fit_ml_null <- doas(
  survey_dat,
  method    = "ML",
  obs_type  = "independent",
  pooling   = "hybrid",
  p_formula = ~ 1,
  n_formula = ~ habitat
)

summary(fit_ml_cov)
cat("True simulated population:", pop$tot_pop, "\n")
QAIC(fit_ml_cov, fit_ml_null)

# Predict detection probability and expected abundance across a covariate gradient
new_sectors <- data.frame(effort = c(-1, 0, 1), habitat = c(-1, 0, 1))
predict(fit_ml_cov, newdata = new_sectors, type = "detection")
predict(fit_ml_cov, newdata = new_sectors, type = "abundance")

# 3. Multi-Chain Hierarchical Bayesian Estimation & WAIC Selection
fit_bayes_null <- doas(
  survey_dat,
  method   = "Bayes",
  obs_type = "independent",
  pooling  = "hybrid",
  chains   = 3,
  iter     = 2000,
  burnin   = 500
)

fit_bayes_cov <- doas(
  survey_dat,
  method    = "Bayes",
  obs_type  = "independent",
  pooling   = "hybrid",
  p_formula = ~ effort,
  n_formula = ~ habitat,
  chains    = 3,
  iter      = 2000,
  burnin    = 500
)

summary(fit_bayes_cov)
WAIC(fit_bayes_null, fit_bayes_cov)

Documentation & Tutorials

A step-by-step tutorial vignette covering field data preparation, frequentist and Bayesian estimation, covariate selection, and prospective power analysis is included with the package:

vignette("DOAS-tutorial", package = "DOAS")

Citation & Methods

If you use DOAS in your research, please cite both the R package and the original methodological paper introducing the Double Observer Adjusted Survey framework:

von Hardenberg, A. (2026). DOAS: Double Observer Adjusted Survey Framework. R package version 0.1.0. https://github.com/achazhardenberg/DOAS

Panaccio, M., Brambilla, A., Bassano, B., Smith, T., & von Hardenberg, A. (2024). A new double observer-based census framework to improve abundance estimations in mountain ungulates and other gregarious species with a reduced effort. Ecological Solutions and Evidence, 5(4), e12405. https://doi.org/10.1002/2688-8319.12405
